sections.h2: How should a Marietta owner approach a sale?
sections.html:
Owners here usually pick between an agent listing, a self-managed sale and a straight cash purchase. Repair needs and your calendar decide which of the three fits.

  • Agent listing: reaches buyers who rely on mortgages, which means showings, inspection requests and a closing date set by their lender.
  • For sale by owner: the agent's share stays with you, and so do pricing, marketing and negotiation.
  • Cash buyer: a quicker close without a repair list, at a price that reflects current condition.

With typical home values listed at $448,500, a small gap in percentage between two offers is a large gap in cash. Get each offer's terms in writing before comparing.

sections.h2: How big is Marietta, and what is its housing like?
sections.html:
Marietta's population estimate for mid-2025 is 63,574, a 4.1% rise over the 61,060 used as the 2020 starting point. Headcounts were 56,579 in 2010 and 60,972 in 2020. The land area is 23.43 square miles, giving 2,602 people for each square mile in the 2020 count.

  • Owners live in 47.2% of homes (2020 to 2024), so renters or other non-owner households occupy the remaining share.
  • Monthly owner costs: $2,170 with a mortgage, $618 without.
  • Median gross rent: $1,586.
  • Households: 24,707, at 2.40 persons each.
  • Adults holding at least a bachelor's degree: 47.4%.
  • Average commute: 27.5 minutes.

Health care stands out in the city's economy. For 2022 the Census lists 3,634,864 thousand dollars in revenue for that sector, against 2,822,793 thousand dollars in retail sales. The city also counts 2,412 veterans among its residents for 2020 to 2024.

sections.h2: How did Marietta grow into the city it is?
sections.html:
The city's own history page traces Marietta back to a small cluster of homes near the Cherokee town of Kennesaw, reported as early as 1824. The Georgia legislature legally recognized the town on December 19, 1834, and Marietta was named for the wife of the man who gave Cobb County its name.

The Western and Atlantic Railroad shaped the early economy. Marietta served as home base for the railroad project, boosting business around the Square, and the town incorporated in 1852. Its Civil War story is just as well known: the raiders of the Great Locomotive Chase gathered in Marietta in April 1862, and in the summer of 1864 forces under William Tecumseh Sherman occupied the town for five months, ending with the burning of the town that November.

The Marietta History Center operates in the historic Kennesaw House. Code Enforcement covers the city's historic district along with zoning and signs, and the city's home page features the historic Church-Cherokee district. Owners of older houses should ask the city which exterior changes need approval before promising a buyer any work.

sections.h2: What building and code rules apply to a Marietta house?
sections.html:
The City of Marietta enforces the 2024 editions of the International Building Code and International Residential Code, with 2026 Georgia amendments, for projects permitted after January 1, 2026. Plumbing, mechanical and fuel gas codes follow the 2024 editions as well, and the electrical code is the 2023 National Electrical Code with 2026 Georgia amendments.

The city asks that all building permits be submitted online. Pulling a permit before repairs matters at sale time, because a buyer's inspector or title review may turn up unpermitted work. The Building Inspection Division can be reached at 770-794-5659.

Code Enforcement checks building code, zoning regulations, signs, the historic district and the standard housing code. It sits at 205 Lawrence Street, with phone 770-794-5439, and it can act only on properties inside the city limits. A Marietta mailing address does not guarantee the house is inside the city, so use the city's Property Search Tool to confirm before you assume which rules apply.

sections.h2: How does Cobb County property tax work when selling in Marietta?
sections.html:
Cobb's Tax Commissioner handles billing for the county government and the school district. The seven cities inside Cobb, Marietta among them, run their own billing, so ask the City of Marietta about its separate portion.

Cobb tax-year milestones from the Tax Commissioner's FAQ
ItemRule
Assessment dateEach January 1 sets who owes for the year
Returns for personal propertyDue at the Tax Assessor's office by April 1
Bills mailedBy August 15
Payment dueOn or before October 15
Late payment5% penalty plus monthly interest

Cobb's office stays out of any split between seller and buyer. Who owes what is set by the closing paperwork, and the purchaser generally takes on the liability. The tax is figured for the full year and follows the property.

The Tax Commissioner does accept partial payments, and it will honor a U.S. Post Office postmark dated by midnight of the deadline, although metered or kiosk postage does not count. An owner appealing a value must still pay at least the appeal amount by the due date. Payment is at 736 Whitlock Avenue, Suite 100, Marietta, or by mail to PO Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061; the office phone is 770-528-8600. The county also notes that 2026 bills carried a state Homeowner Tax Relief Grant, separate from homestead exemptions.

Drop boxes sit outside the Whitlock Avenue office, and the East Cobb and South Cobb Government Service Centers also take payments. Anyone buying a Marietta house can try the Tax Commissioner's estimator for new home purchasers, where you enter a fair market value, choose the city or unincorporated tax district and select exemptions. The tool applies the 40% assessed value rule from O.C.G.A. 48-5-7 and covers county taxes only, so a buyer still has to ask the city for its own figure. Sellers can use it too, to explain to a buyer what the county side of the bill is likely to look like.

sections.h2: What happens if Cobb property taxes go unpaid before a Marietta sale?
sections.html:
Cobb's Tax Commissioner says that after the last day for payment it notifies the taxpayer in writing, and unless the taxes are paid within thirty days an execution, called a fi. fa., may be issued under O.C.G.A. 48-3-3. Taxes legally attach to the property, so settle any balance early.

Tax sales run on the first Tuesday of each month in which a sale is planned, held on the Superior Courthouse steps at Flournoy Park in Marietta between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Cobb publishes a Tax Sale Booklet on the process. If you are behind, call 770-528-8600 about payment arrangements before the sale date, since the office accepts partial payments though penalty and interest continue to accrue on the balance.

sections.h2: What does recording a Marietta deed involve?
sections.html:
The Cobb clerk records the deed only after the state transfer tax is paid and a PT-61 is filed. Georgia's rate is $1 on the first $1,000 or any fraction of it, and 10 cents on each further $100 or fraction of $100.

Legal liability sits with the seller unless the contract moves it. After the sale, the new owner will need the recorded deed to reapply for a homestead exemption, according to the Tax Commissioner.

faqs.q: Who covers Cobb property tax when a Marietta house closes?
faqs.a: The contract and settlement statement decide. The Tax Commissioner does not prorate between the parties, and liability generally passes to the purchaser.

faqs.q: What is the payment deadline on a Cobb tax bill?
faqs.a: October 15, with bills mailed by August 15. After that a 5% penalty applies and interest builds monthly. Marietta's own city bill is separate, so ask the city for that date.

faqs.q: Can I get a Marietta building permit online?
faqs.a: Yes. The city asks that all permits be submitted online, and its Building Inspection Division at 770-794-5659 can answer questions. Code Enforcement at 770-794-5439 handles complaints inside city limits only.

faqs.q: Is every Marietta mailing address inside city limits?
faqs.a: Not always. The city's Code Enforcement page warns that a Marietta mailing address does not place a property inside the limits. The city's Property Search Tool shows which government's rules apply.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It ends. Cobb asks owners who no longer qualify, including those who sold or moved, to tell the Tax Commissioner, and failing to report can bring a penalty. The buyer applies separately.
